config.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled

intro.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with two input fields to explore the difference between controlled and uncontrolled components in React. You will learn how React manages form data by comparing state-driven controlled inputs with directly accessed uncontrolled ones. The core concepts involve using React's useState hook for controlled components and the useRef hook to access DOM elements for uncontrolled components. You will implement both patterns in TypeScript, ensuring type safety for your input values and references. By the end, you'll understand when to use each approach for handling form data in your applications.
intro.usecase: Understanding controlled vs uncontrolled components is essential when building interactive forms in applications like user registration, checkout flows, or settings panels. In a controlled approach, React manages form state—ideal for real-time validation in sign-up forms where each keystroke must be validated. Uncontrolled components are useful for file upload inputs or search filters where you only need the final value on submission. This distinction helps developers choose the right pattern for scenarios like dashboard filters (controlled for immediate UI updates) versus simple contact forms (uncontrolled for less overhead).

objectives: Apply the useState hook to declare and initialize a state variable for a controlled input.
Construct a controlled input component by assigning the state variable to the input's value attribute.
Implement an event handler function to update the state variable when the input's onChange event fires.
Define an uncontrolled input component by using the useRef hook to create a mutable reference.
Access the current value of an uncontrolled input by retrieving the ref's .current.value property.
Utilize the useEffect hook to perform side effects, such as logging, when an uncontrolled input's value changes.
Compare the rendered output of a controlled and uncontrolled input to observe their behavioral differences.
Modify a form component to conditionally switch between controlled and uncontrolled input rendering based on state.
Execute a form submission handler that retrieves and processes values from both controlled and uncontrolled inputs.
Store user input data from a controlled input into a parent component's state via a callback prop.
Handle input validation by applying conditional logic within the onChange handler of a controlled component.
Return a React component that demonstrates both patterns side-by-side with clear visual separation.

steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in the component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there might be a small issue. Check that you're importing both React and useState from 'react' with the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Remember to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ControlledVsUncontrolled that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name ControlledVsUncontrolled that returns null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the ControlledVsUncontrolled component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named ControlledVsUncontrolled is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The component is defined with the correct name and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main component. It's ready to be built upon in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named exactly 'ControlledVsUncontrolled' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you used the exact name 'ControlledVsUncontrolled' and that it returns null.

steps.title: Initialize controlled input state
steps.instruction: Inside your ControlledVsUncontrolled component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'controlledValue' initialized to an empty string.
steps.hint: Remember to call useState with the initial value (empty string) and destructure the returned array into the value and setter.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing a string state variable
const [text, setText] = useState<string>('');
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a state variable 'controlledValue' and its setter 'setControlledValue' available for use in the component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the controlled input state. The 'controlledValue' variable will hold the current value of the controlled input, and 'setControlledValue' will update it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're using useState correctly. Make sure you're destructuring both the value and setter, naming them 'controlledValue' and 'setControlledValue', and initializing with an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to call useState with an empty string as the initial value, then destructure the returned array into 'controlledValue' and 'setControlledValue'.

steps.title: Define controlled input change handler
steps.instruction: Inside your ControlledVsUncontrolled component, define a function named handleControlledChange that takes an event parameter and updates the controlledValue state with the input's current value.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> and calls setControlledValue with event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleControlledChange function that properly handles input change events and updates the controlledValue state.
successCriteria: The function should be named handleControlledChange, accept an event parameter of type React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>, and call setControlledValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleControlledChange function. This is the event handler that will update the controlled input's state whenever the user types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are some issues. Make sure your function is named handleControlledChange, accepts an event parameter with the correct type, and calls setControlledValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleControlledChange function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function that takes an event parameter and updates the controlledValue state with the input's value.

steps.title: Create uncontrolled input ref
steps.instruction: Inside your component, create a ref named 'uncontrolledInputRef' using the useRef hook. Type the ref to hold either an HTMLInputElement or null.
steps.hint: You'll need to call useRef with an initial value of null and specify the generic type.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a ref ready to be attached to an uncontrolled input element in a future step.
successCriteria: The code should include a call to useRef with the correct generic type and initial value, assigned to a variable named uncontrolledInputRef.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed ref for the uncontrolled input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you name the ref 'uncontrolledInputRef'? Did you specify the type HTMLInputElement | null?
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a ref using useRef, typed to hold an HTMLInputElement or null, and name it uncontrolledInputRef.

steps.title: Define uncontrolled input handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleUncontrolledSubmit that reads the current value from uncontrolledInputRef and logs it to the console.
steps.hint: Create a function that accesses the ref's current value property. Remember to use the ref name defined in the previous step.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named handleUncontrolledSubmit is defined that reads the value from uncontrolledInputRef.
successCriteria: The function should be defined with the correct name, access uncontrolledInputRef.current?.value, and log it to console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the handler function for the uncontrolled input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the function is named handleUncontrolledSubmit and accesses uncontrolledInputRef.current?.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check the function name and how you access the ref's value.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement, add a main container div with two sections: one for controlled inputs and one for uncontrolled inputs.
steps.hint: Create a <div> inside the existing outer div, then add two <section> elements inside it with appropriate headings.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a structured layout with two distinct sections ready for controlled and uncontrolled input examples.
successCriteria: Include two <section> elements inside that container
Each section should have an <h2> heading
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the basic structure with two sections. This provides clear visual separation for our controlled and uncontrolled examples.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have: 1) A container div after the h1, 2) Two section elements inside it, 3) Each section has an h2 heading.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match what's needed. You should add a container div with two sections, each containing an h2 heading.

steps.title: Add controlled input field
steps.instruction: Inside the main container, add an input element for the controlled section. Set its value to the controlledValue state and its onChange handler to handleControlledChange.
steps.hint: Create an <input> element with value={controlledValue} and onChange={handleControlledChange} attributes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The controlled input field will be added to the component, ready to display and update the controlledValue state.
successCriteria: The input element must have value={controlledValue} and onChange={handleControlledChange} attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a controlled input field that displays the current controlledValue and updates it when the user types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input field, but it's missing either the value or onChange attribute. Make sure to include both value={controlledValue} and onChange={handleControlledChange}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The controlled input field is not properly implemented. Please add an <input> element with both value={controlledValue} and onChange={handleControlledChange} attributes.

steps.title: Display controlled input value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the controlled input field that displays the current controlledValue state. Use JSX curly braces to render the value.
steps.hint:
Create a

tag with the text content showing the controlledValue variable inside curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of displaying a state value in a paragraph

Current value: {controlledValue}
steps.expectedOutcome: The controlled input's current value will be visible in the UI as text below the input field.
successCriteria: Display controlledValue inside the paragraph using JSX curly braces
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a paragraph that displays the current controlled input value. This demonstrates how React state keeps the UI in sync with data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying the controlledValue variable inside the paragraph using JSX curly braces like {controlledValue}.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph isn't displaying the controlled input value correctly. Remember to create a

element and insert the controlledValue variable inside curly braces.

steps.title: Add uncontrolled input field
steps.instruction: Add an input element with ref={uncontrolledInputRef} and no value or onChange props.
steps.hint: Use a standard <input> tag and set its ref attribute to uncontrolledInputRef. Do not add value or onChange props.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of an uncontrolled input with ref
<input type="text" ref={inputRef} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an uncontrolled input field that uses a ref to access its value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added an uncontrolled input field that uses a ref to access its value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an input element with ref={uncontrolledInputRef} and no value or onChange props.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Add an input element with ref={uncontrolledInputRef} and no value or onChange props.

steps.title: Add button to read uncontrolled value
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside your component's return statement. The button should have an onClick handler that calls the handleUncontrolledSubmit function (which you defined earlier). The button text should be 'Read Uncontrolled Value'.
steps.hint: Place the button after the uncontrolled input field. Use the onClick prop with the handler function name.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding a button with an onClick handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Read Uncontrolled Value' appears below the uncontrolled input field. When clicked, it will trigger the handleUncontrolledSubmit function.
successCriteria: Button element with text 'Read Uncontrolled Value'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that will read the uncontrolled input value when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have both: a button with the text 'Read Uncontrolled Value' and the onClick handler set to handleUncontrolledSubmit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't quite right. Check that you've added a button element with the correct text and onClick handler.

steps.title: Add explanatory comments
steps.instruction: Add two comment blocks in your component's JSX: one above the controlled input section explaining how controlled inputs work, and one above the uncontrolled input section explaining how uncontrolled inputs work. Focus on the key differences: state management vs. DOM refs.
steps.hint: Use JSX comments (/* ... */) or regular JavaScript comments (// ...) inside your JSX. Place them right before the <div> containing each input section.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Controlled inputs: React state manages the value, onChange updates state, value prop reflects state */

Controlled Input

/* Uncontrolled inputs: DOM holds the value, ref accesses it on demand, no onChange needed */

Uncontrolled Input
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will now include clear documentation explaining the difference between controlled and uncontrolled inputs directly in the JSX.
successCriteria: The code must contain at least one comment explaining controlled inputs (mentioning state, onChange, value prop) and at least one comment explaining uncontrolled inputs (mentioning ref, DOM access, no onChange). Comments should be placed near the relevant input sections.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your explanatory comments clearly document the key differences between controlled and uncontrolled inputs, making the code more understandable.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some comments, but make sure you have both: one for controlled inputs (mentioning state/onChange/value) and one for uncontrolled inputs (mentioning ref/DOM access). Place them right before each input section.
steps.feedbackWrong: No comments were added. Add two comment blocks: one above the controlled input section explaining how React state manages the value, and one above the uncontrolled input section explaining how DOM refs access the value.
